description: Go language audit heuristics derived from Sigma Prime 'Go for Security Auditors: Part 1 - Syntax That Will Trip You Up' (June 2026). Covers deceptive syntax, common pitfalls, testing gotchas, and compiler pragmas.
review_checklist: Constructors initialize map and slice fields before any write path.
Methods that mutate receiver state use pointer receivers (*T), not value receivers (T).
Error returns use bare nil on success, not typed nil pointers assigned to error.
Background loops and goroutine pools honor context cancellation (ctx.Done()).
Pre-Go-1.22 code: loop variables copied before async closure or t.Parallel subtests.
Security-relevant tests are not gated behind build tags skipped in CI.
Rare //go:noescape, //go:nosplit, //go:linkname pragmas are justified and reviewed.

rules.title: Sparse composite literal with index gaps
rules.summary: Index-keyed array literals zero-fill skipped slots; miscounted wire or crypto layouts get silent padding.
rules.trigger: Composite literal uses explicit index keys (e.g. 3: value) in byte or int arrays.
rules.rationale: Unexpected zeros in packed structures break signature verification or parsing without compile-time errors.
rules.actionable_check: Verify every index against the wire spec; prefer sequential literals or named constants for protocol fields.
rules.graph_hint: function builds fixed-size buffer or array literal

rules.title: Shared type declaration hides parameter kinds
rules.summary: Consecutive parameters sharing one type are easy to misread during review; copy-paste can inherit wrong types.
rules.trigger: Function signature lists multiple identifiers before a single type name.
rules.rationale: Security-sensitive verify/compare helpers may accidentally treat distinct parameters as the same kind.
rules.actionable_check: Re-read signatures slowly; confirm each parameter type matches intent (especially []byte triples).
rules.graph_hint: function with three or more parameters sharing one type token

rules.title: Loop index discarded where position matters
rules.summary: for _, item := range coll discards index; logic that depends on position may be wrong or rely on side effects.
rules.trigger: range loop uses _ for index while body references ordering, parity, or positional invariants.
rules.rationale: Off-by-one and wrong-element selection bugs hide when index should gate behavior.
rules.actionable_check: If order or index affects correctness, bind the index and validate it explicitly.
rules.graph_hint: range loop with blank index identifier

rules.title: Goroutine or closure captures loop variable by reference
rules.summary: Closures spawned inside loops capture the loop variable by reference; pre-Go-1.22 code prints or uses the final value for every iteration.
rules.trigger: go func() or defer func() inside for/range without per-iteration copy of loop variable.
rules.rationale: All goroutines may observe the same variable after the loop finishes, causing wrong IDs, races, or duplicated work.
rules.actionable_check: Copy loop variable inside the body (i := i) on pre-1.22 toolchains; verify go.mod go version.
rules.graph_hint: goroutine spawn inside loop header region

rules.title: Mutating method uses value receiver instead of pointer
rules.summary: Methods on T operate on a copy; mutations to flags, counters, or locks on the copy are discarded.
rules.trigger: Method receiver is (s Type) not (s *Type) but body assigns to s fields or calls lock methods on s.
rules.rationale: Security checks or config updates silently fail when callers expect persisted state changes.
rules.actionable_check: Use pointer receiver (*Type) when the method mutates receiver fields or holds locks.
rules.graph_hint: method node with value receiver and mutation edges

rules.title: Bare for loop without context cancellation path
rules.summary: for { select { ... } } event loops must exit on ctx.Done(); missing cancellation leaks goroutines and capacity.
rules.trigger: Infinite for/select loop serving HTTP, gRPC, libp2p, or worker queues lacks ctx.Done() branch.
rules.rationale: Unbounded loops ignore shutdown signals and become DoS or resource-exhaustion vectors.
rules.actionable_check: Trace every exit path; wire context through listeners and background workers.
rules.graph_hint: function contains for-without-condition and channel receive

rules.title: Write to nil map field without constructor init
rules.summary: Struct map fields default to nil; reads work but writes panic. Tests that only read hide the crash path.
rules.trigger: Assignment to map field on struct whose constructor never allocates the map.
rules.rationale: Production inputs that first hit a write path crash the process (consensus nodes, bridges, validators).
rules.actionable_check: Initialize maps in constructors (make or literal); audit all map fields on config/state structs.
rules.graph_hint: struct field map[string]T written before make

rules.title: Slice shares backing array with sensitive or shared buffer
rules.summary: Sub-slices alias memory; append with spare capacity mutates siblings; zeroing one slice may not clear copies.
rules.trigger: Slice derived from another via [low:high] then append or mutation in concurrent or crypto code.
rules.rationale: Secret material or shared state corrupts across goroutines when append reuses capacity in place.
rules.actionable_check: Copy with append([]T(nil), src...) or copy() when isolation is required; cap-aware review of append.
rules.graph_hint: slice expression followed by append on shared buffer

rules.title: Defer evaluates arguments immediately, not at return
rules.summary: defer log.Printf("took %v", time.Since(start)) logs zero duration because Since ran at defer registration.
rules.trigger: defer call passes time.Since, len, or other call expressions meant to run at function exit.
rules.rationale: Broken metrics and misleading audit logs hide timing attacks or failed cleanup ordering.
rules.actionable_check: Wrap deferred work in func() { ... }() so evaluation happens on return.
rules.graph_hint: defer statement with non-literal call arguments

rules.title: Typed nil pointer returned as error interface
rules.summary: Returning var err *MyError = nil as error yields non-nil interface (type set, value nil); err != nil is true.
rules.trigger: Function returns named typed error pointer that may stay nil instead of bare return nil.
rules.rationale: Callers skip error handling or take wrong branches when success paths appear as failures or vice versa.
rules.actionable_check: Return bare nil on success; avoid returning typed nil pointers through error interface.
rules.graph_hint: function return type error with typed error variable

rules.title: Variable shadowing or stale err in error wrap
rules.summary: := inside if shadows outer err; fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err) after failed type assert may wrap wrong/nil err.
rules.trigger: Short variable declaration reuses err name, or fmt.Errorf wraps err not set by the failing branch.
rules.rationale: Misleading error chains hide root cause and break security monitoring or rollback decisions.
rules.actionable_check: Run go vet -shadow; ensure each error wrap uses the err from the immediately preceding failure.

rules.title: Parallel subtests without per-case loop copy (pre-1.22)
rules.summary: t.Parallel inside table-driven subtests without tc := tc runs the last case repeatedly.
rules.trigger: for _, tc := range cases { t.Run(..., func(t *testing.T) { t.Parallel() ...}) } without inner copy.
rules.rationale: Tests pass while failing to exercise claimed cases; security regressions ship undetected.
rules.actionable_check: Add tc := tc before t.Run on pre-1.22; confirm go.mod version and CI Go toolchain.
rules.graph_hint: test function with t.Parallel in nested closure

rules.title: Security tests gated by build tags skipped in CI
rules.summary: //go:build integration or !prod excludes tests unless CI passes -tags; security checks may never run.
rules.trigger: Test files carry build tags like integration, fuzz, or negated prod without matching CI invocation.
rules.rationale: Tagged security tests give false confidence when default go test omits them.
rules.actionable_check: Audit CI for tag matrix; run go test -tags integration (and prod variants) in review.
rules.graph_hint: test file with go:build constraint comment

rules.title: Table-driven tests omit error and boundary rows
rules.summary: Large happy-path tables create review false confidence; malformed input and error branches absent.
rules.trigger: Table struct lists only success cases for parser, auth, or crypto validation entrypoints.
rules.rationale: Attack surface inputs never exercised despite comprehensive-looking test scaffolding.
rules.actionable_check: Extend tables with empty, max, malformed, and permission-denied cases; review table contents not shape.
rules.graph_hint: Test* function with tests slice lacking wantErr rows

rules.title: Internal invariants only tested via external test package
rules.summary: package foo_test cannot access unexported helpers; subtle internal bugs need white-box *_test.go in same package.
rules.trigger: All tests use package mypkg_test with no same-package test files for sensitive internals.
rules.rationale: Critical invariants on unexported state may lack direct coverage during security review.
rules.actionable_check: Look for impl_test.go in package mypkg alongside mypkg_test black-box tests.
rules.graph_hint: test package name ends with _test suffix only

rules.title: Unsafe //go:noescape annotation may hide stack escape bugs
rules.summary: Incorrect //go:noescape lets pointers escape to heap or be used after stack frame ends (use-after-free).
rules.trigger: Function preceded by //go:noescape with pointer parameters or returns.
rules.rationale: Wrong escape analysis in otherwise safe Go yields memory corruption at runtime.
rules.actionable_check: Prove pointer lifetimes; prefer safe APIs; treat pragma as expert-only with comment justification.

rules.title: //go:nosplit disables stack growth on deep or recursive paths
rules.summary: nosplit functions cannot grow stack; deep call chains overflow instead of expanding safely.
rules.trigger: //go:nosplit on functions that recurse or call deep runtime chains.
rules.rationale: Stack overflow crashes service goroutines handling untrusted input.
rules.actionable_check: Verify bounded stack use; document why nosplit is required (often runtime internals only).

rules.title: //go:linkname breaks package encapsulation
rules.summary: linkname imports unexported symbols across packages; bypasses visibility and stability guarantees.
rules.trigger: Source contains //go:linkname directive referencing foreign package symbols.
rules.rationale: Hidden dependencies on runtime internals break across Go releases and hide dangerous calls.
rules.actionable_check: Treat as high scrutiny; confirm upstream stability and absence of safer public API.
rules.graph_hint: linkname directive edge to unexported symbol
